idea-plugin.name: insrc
idea-plugin.description:
insrc brings the insrc code-knowledge system into the JetBrains IDE family — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm — from a single install. It is a thin orchestrator that owns no reasoning of its own: it wires insrc's grounded-analyze and tracked-workflow capabilities into the IDE's own AI assistant and manages the backing daemon, so your assistant answers from a citation-grounded model of your codebase rather than guessing.

What it does

  • One integration, four IDEs. A single artifact activates identically in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm.
  • Wires your AI host automatically. On project open it detects your agentic assistant (JetBrains AI Assistant or Junie) and registers the insrc MCP server plus the tracked-workflow steering into that host's own configuration.
  • One-click project enablement. An "Enable insrc for this project" prompt registers the open project with the insrc daemon; every capability call is scoped to that project's path.
  • Manages the backing daemon. Ensures the daemon is present and current, provisioning a private Node runtime when the system one is missing — first-time setup is a single explicit consent, updates are silent.
  • Grounded analyze + tracked workflow. Your assistant explores the code through a citation-grounded graph, and features route through insrc's tracked design → review → plan → build workflow.
  • Clean and reversible. All writes into host config/rules files are marker-delimited and preserve your own content; uninstalling the plugin removes exactly those blocks, while a mere disable leaves them intact.

Privacy

The plugin opens no cloud path and stores no credentials — all reasoning runs through your assistant's existing CLI/OAuth sessions.

Requirements

  • A JetBrains AI host (AI Assistant or Junie) — without one the plugin stays dormant and re-checks on later project opens.
  • Node (used by the daemon); the plugin provisions a private runtime automatically if the system Node is unsuitable.
  • The insrc daemon, which the plugin installs on first use.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1

  • Compatibility: removed the upper IDE-build bound — the plugin now loads on current and future IDE releases (2024.2 and later), since it depends only on the stable platform module.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Single-artifact activation across IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm.
  • AI-host detection (AI Assistant / Junie) with automatic MCP-server and tracked-workflow steering registration.
  • One-click project registration against the insrc daemon.
  • Daemon lifecycle management: presence/staleness check, consented first-time setup, tiered Node runtime.
  • Clean, reversible uninstall of all host-file writes.
